newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures seen opening flat to higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures seen opening flat to higher.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures are called to open flat to higher following Tuesday's rise tied to outlook of heating demand in the Northwest and a rally in natural gas prices, industry sources said.
In early over-the-counter (OTC) activity, November California-Oregon Border (COB) futures were discussed at $17.25-$17.50 a megawatt hour (MWh) and November OTC Palo Verde (PV) $16.70-$16.80.
While most of the Northwest was expected to reach 30s to 40s degree Fahrenheit in the night hours, scattered parts of the region were forecast to experience weather in the teens.
Meanwhile, the Southwest was predicted to enjoy mild autumn temperatures through the end of the week.
Brokers and traders noted November COB need to breach $17.50 and November PV $17.00 to continue Tuesday's climb.
In Tuesday's ACCESS session, November COB was last bid at $17.00 against a settlement of $17.40, and November PV futures were left unchanged at $16.85.
